posts.text: NEW research from Sakana AI. Long contexts get expensive as every token in the input contributes to quadratic attention costs, higher latency, and more memory. This new research introduces Doc-to-LoRA, a lightweight hypernetwork that meta-learns to compress long documents into LoRA adapters in a SINGLE forward pass. In other words, it can instantly internalize contexts. Instead of re-reading the full context at every inference call, the model internalizes the document into compact adapter weights. No iterative fine-tuning is needed, and no repeated context consumption. Results: near-perfect accuracy on needle-in-a-haystack tasks at sequence lengths exceeding the target model's native context window by over 4x. Outperforms standard context distillation while significantly reducing peak memory consumption and update latency on real-world QA datasets. Why it matters: turning context into compact adapters on the fly could drastically reduce serving costs and enable rapid knowledge updates.
posts.notes: Sakana AI Doc-to-LoRA: hypernetwork compresses documents into LoRA adapters in single forward pass. 4x context extension, near-perfect needle-in-haystack. Cost reduction lever for long-context agents. 220 bookmarks.

posts.text: How good are AI agents at long-horizon CLI programming? Not very. Leading agents succeed less than 20% of the time. LongCLI-Bench introduces a benchmark of 20 complex tasks spanning building from scratch, adding features, fixing bugs, and refactoring code, all executed through command-line interfaces. Failures typically occur early in task execution. Self-correction provides minimal improvement. But human-agent collaboration through plan guidance and interactive input substantially enhances performance. Why does it matter? The benchmark highlights that for real-world programming tasks, the path forward isn't fully autonomous agents. It's human-agent collaboration with structured oversight.
posts.notes: LongCLI-Bench: leading agents <20% success on long-horizon CLI programming. Failures happen early, self-correction minimal, human-agent collaboration substantially improves outcomes. Validates orchestrator-in-loop architecture vs full autonomy.

posts.text: NEW research from Meta Superintelligence Labs. It uses a clever strategy-auction framework to improve self-improving agents on complex tasks. Small agents aren't always enough. On the simplest tasks, a 4B parameter agent attains 87% of a 32B agent's performance. But on the hardest tasks, the gap widens dramatically. SALE: on deep search tasks, exceeds best single agent pass@1 by 3.5 points while reducing cost by 35%. On coding tasks, improves pass@1 by 2.7 points at 25% lower cost.
posts.notes: SALE paper (Meta SuperIntelligence Labs): strategy-auction framework for self-improving agents. 3.5pt improvement + 35% cost reduction on deep search. 2.7pt + 25% cost reduction on coding. Validates multi-agent coordination economics. 271 bookmarks.

posts.text: NEW research on improving memory for AI Agents. (bookmark it) As context windows scale to millions of tokens, the bottleneck shifts from raw capacity to cognitive control. Knowing what you know, knowing what's missing, and knowing when to stop matters more than processing every token. This paper introduces InfMem, a bounded-memory agent using PRETHINK–RETRIEVE–WRITE protocol, maintaining accuracy up to 1M tokens while reducing inference latency by 3.9x.
posts.notes: InfMem paper: bounded-memory agent, PRETHINK–RETRIEVE–WRITE protocol. 3.9x latency reduction, accurate at 1M tokens. Key insight: cognitive control > raw context capacity. 260 bookmarks.

posts.text: New research from Google DeepMind. Really good read to understand what's ahead with AI agents. It introduces a comprehensive framework for intelligent AI delegation, a sequence of decisions involving task allocation that also incorporates transfer of authority, responsibility, accountability, clear role specifications, and mechanisms for establishing trust between parties. Why does it matter? As AI agents move from isolated assistants to participants in complex delegation networks and virtual economies, the absence of robust delegation protocols introduces significant societal risks.
posts.notes: Google DeepMind AI Delegation Framework. 160K views, 2,391 bookmarks — highest engagement in Feb omarsar0 set. Covers task allocation, authority transfer, accountability, trust establishment. Critical framework for agentic web protocol design. Directly relevant to A2A and orchestration architecture.

posts.text: New research from Google DeepMind. What if LLMs could discover entirely new multi-agent learning algorithms? Designing algorithms for multi-agent systems is hard. Classic approaches like PSRO and counterfactual regret minimization took years of expert effort to develop. This research uses LLMs to automatically generate novel multi-agent learning algorithms through iterative prompting and refinement. The LLM proposes algorithm pseudocode, which gets evaluated against game-theoretic benchmarks. The discovered algorithms achieve competitive performance against established hand-crafted baselines.
posts.notes: Google DeepMind LLM-discovered multi-agent algorithms. LLMs as creative search engines over algorithm space — competitive with hand-crafted baselines. 374 bookmarks. Shifts algorithm design from expert craft to automated discovery.

posts.text: New research from Intuit AI Research. Agent performance depends on more than just the agent. It also depends on the quality of the tool descriptions it reads. However, tool interfaces are still written for humans, not LLMs. As the number of candidate tools grows, poor descriptions become a real bottleneck for tool selection and parameter generation. This new research introduces Trace-Free+, a curriculum learning framework that teaches models to rewrite tool descriptions into versions that are more effective for LLM agents.
posts.notes: Trace-Free+ paper: curriculum learning for better tool descriptions. Key insight: optimize tool interface itself, not just the agent. Practical lever for improving agent reliability at scale.
